independent_kernel.note: Independently written kernel ('external checker'). Its deliberate divergences from the C++ kernel are documented upstream in divergences.md; notably it does not implement reduceBool, so native evaluation cannot be reduced by it.
independent_kernel.link_note: lake's link step fails on this machine (the conda build records placeholder library paths); linked with system gcc via relink.py.

limits.export_mem_note: RLIMIT_AS caps address space, not resident memory; `lean --run` (the exporter) mmaps the whole Lean library plus the interpreter and needs more reserved address space than a submission compile. CPU, wall clock, file size and the unprivileged user still apply.
limits.resource_exhaustion_note: A checker killed by the CPU, wall-clock or memory limit has NOT rejected the proof. The driver classifies 124 / -24 / -9 / 137 / TIMEOUT as resource exhaustion and reports the claim INCONCLUSIVE (never certified, but not a rejection either). Found while verifying the package: two concurrent pytest sessions on this 2-core machine were enough to make lean4lean hit the CPU limit on the largest submission, and the earlier code read that as a kernel rejection -- a verdict that depended on machine load.

third_check.provenance: NOT written by this round's author: it appeared in harness/ mid-session, unreviewed, and was moved out of the trusted path. Reviewed line by line and fixed by this round's author; verdict and findings in harness/kernel3/REVIEW.md. The unmodified original is kept in unreviewed/kernel/ for comparison.
third_check.independence: shares no code with Lean and does not use Lean's elaborator; it reads an exported closure and re-derives every type itself
third_check.covers: every declaration's type; inductive specifications only where their fingerprint matches reference/kernel_baseline.json
third_check.does_not_cover: the legitimacy of an inductive specification (strict positivity, the shape of the generated recursor and its iota rules). Two hand-written forgeries that prove False through that hole are kept as test vectors in tests/forgeries/; the provenance gate reports them instead of vouching for them.
third_check.gate: an error fails certification; introduced_assumptions do not block (that layer is covered by the two Lean-based kernels) but are recorded in the evidence
